title: Part Two: Why There Is a Vatican: 754 to 1929

sections.brief: The Papal States 754-1870: Stephen II and Pippin (754 promise, 756 grant; not 752), the Donation of Constantine forgery and Valla 1440, extent (44,000 km2, 3.1m in 1853) and clerical government, Albornoz 1357, Napoleon 1809, Vienna 1815, 1848-49 Roman Republic and French restoration, 1860 losses. Figures: time

Porta Pia 20 September 1870, the Law of Guarantees 13 May 1871 and Pius IX's rejection (Ubi Nos, endowment refused), the prisoner years 1870-1929, non expedit and the PPI 1919, two misreadings corrected, 25 July 1929 procession. Figures: compare (1871 law vs 1929 treaty)

11 February 1929: Pius XI's stated motives (11 and 13 Feb allocutions), Mussolini's (Kertzer, treaty Art. 26), negotiation by Francesco Pacelli with Gasparri, the PPI dissolved 5 Nov 1926 (not the Centre Party, not by the Pacts), Concordat Art. 43 and the 1931 Catholic Action clash, the Financial Convention (750m lire cash + 1bn lire 5% bonds; no £30M), Nogara's Special Administration, control then vs now (Fundamental Laws 2023 and 31 July 2026), Art. 24 neutrality. Figures: money (Financial Convention); compare (control 1929 vs Oct 2026)
